title: Clarify compiler-input closure and the exact two-command consumer domain
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Archive the completed compiler-input scope correction from Pro, its independent criterion review, and a subsequent exact original-source consumer-domain proof in the new isolated `research/h25-c05-criterion-consumer-contract` package.

compiler-input closure requires an independently approved bounded witness for the named current header/search/macro/compiler/specs/link/library closure. A 21-channel universal-origin enclosure is an optional sufficient method; its stronger obligations are not prerequisites for every alternative construction. This correction establishes no current simpler adequate implementation, inventory completeness or row saving.

The actual direct variant consumer has exactly two ordered `-nostartfiles` role builds, `pyinit_failure` and `exec_failure`, with six literal C/header path occurrences and the same GCC options in both Python modes. It never calls `native_packet.prepare`. The original positive triple is a separate linked consumer/contract without `-nostartfiles`; there is no automatic five-command child-compiler-input closure union. The header-admission SHA is a copied provenance binding, not completeness authority, and the parent's nine-category/8192-row inventory is separate. Parent cwd C0 is independently fixed; the helper inherits actual producer cwd/environment, whose continuity remains open.

`C5(D,Gamma)` and Gamma must be fixed/admitted independently of the proposed inventory or favorable queries. The sufficient inclusion into `JustifiedFacts(I,Pi;Gamma)` requires explicit sound rules, provenance, bounded representation and current-instance binding; Pi cannot be an off-inventory oracle. Intended complete builds and admitted variation keep the domain nonvacuous despite proper early-refusal controls.

Full compiler-input closure and the full bootstrap-control campaign remain false. All costs remain `OPEN_NOT_ZERO`. No selected-frontier, supplier, theorem, full-caller or performance result is proposed.

## Task and overlap

Original source investigation: [PR #6321](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6321). Frozen H25 benchmark: [PR #6029](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6029). Immediate predecessors: [PR #6377](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6377), [PR #6379](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6379).

Explicit donor source-clarification assignment; scope **refined** because Pro corrected the earlier universal-enclosure framing and the source proof resolves the exact direct consumer. No task picker/card was run. Base `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, tree `e6898c8ba7a27b71587c32ba3f639259ceeeed91`, live-main observation 2026-11-02 20:18:55 UTC. The older original source basis is intentionally retained byte for byte in inert `.py.txt` snapshots with exact path/byte/SHA256/Git-blob mapping.

Bounded overlap checked the first 30 open PRs by update at 20:23:46 UTC and the known retained 36-node dependency graph. Relevant unchanged heads: [PR6377](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6377) `2a26450dea25d7648b585befce5ed375857a8f90` (Linux channel source audit); [PR6379](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6379) `48e99ca2be58cd455f1d56896e9deea6652e5308` (conditional AT_RANDOM events); [PR6374](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6374) `b02bfe3338f7fe57818262b33f8e5c77ac0f1c93` (owned-directory preparation); [PR6373](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6373) `b91c5c74f252c1a98ab8344d012702170004ed13` (bounded caller). This later criterion/domain clarification is additive and edits none of them. A compiler-input closure search returned zero despite listed known matches, so its empty result is non-authoritative; no global novelty/exhaustive-coverage claim is made.

## Validation

The documented source-archive format is deliberate. No `VERIFY.json` hook executes the unqualified originals. The standalone new `verify_integrity.py` checks complete archive file inventory, exact bytes/SHA256/Git-blob identity, source mapping, structured-witness consistency and selected literal contract anchors; it reads text/JSON only, imports no archived code, invokes no subprocess and writes no package files.

Observed local checks passed with Python 3 standard library in normal and `-O` modes, and from a Git-free read-only package-only copy. A copied Pro consultation response with one added byte was rejected. Commands:

```sh
python3 -B research/h25-c05-criterion-consumer-contract/verify_integrity.py
python3 -O -B research/h25-c05-criterion-consumer-contract/verify_integrity.py
```

The exact Pro answer is 8,312 bytes, SHA256 `25b826a0c3160961bd837694e350403f6a61e7ee526a68b8f5c5e2174110df32`; completion receipt and both independent audit reports are retained. There are no claimed Pro consultation attachments or prompt/history exports. All original source snapshots are inert; the archive is self-contained for this static audit, not an executable transitive-source closure or full-history claim. A shared Git cache is not source-history evidence. Hosted plan success with replay skipped would establish archival planning only.

No GCC/diagnostic/native/TCB/original baseline/bootstrap-control campaign/policy/namespace operation was run or admitted. No fitting inventory, source-to-installed correspondence, current namespace/C07 lifetime, genuine configured parent/native/receiver/funding admission, fixed C06 expectations or complete-cost original execution is supplied. Static source proof, byte integrity, AI review, publication and any later archival merge remain distinct.

## Credit

Chris R/Clear1nsight retain original contribution credit; substantial OpenAI Pro, Codex and GPT-6.1 Sol Max assistance is disclosed. Preserve PR6321, PR6029 and PR5864; unpaidmoon and Cursor/Grok assistance associated with PR6339; Douglas R. Colkitt and upstream research/replay maintainers. Exact source notices and Apache-2.0 license are retained. No predecessor gain is inherited and historical native source/finite-route credit is preserved without inventing current admission.

## Open next questions

See the package README's **Open next questions**. The smallest useful follow-up is one concrete command-specific installed-configuration producer-to-consumer contract: independently freeze D/Gamma, map effective include/PCH/macro/specs/subtool/link-selection facts and justified complements to the original consuming path, and bind its reporting/source rules to the exact installed instance. Stop at the precise unavailable installed-default/specs/tool-selection/reporting correspondence; package identity, a successful query or an unverified public-interface premise is insufficient. This archive authorizes no query.

Then, separately: complete inventory construction/fit and current namespace observations; actual cwd/environment continuity and C07 ownership/lifetime; configured source/parent/native/receiver/funding admission and C06 expectations; intact V01 baseline and every original bootstrap-control campaign case in both modes with all original caps/failure rules and complete costs. Those remain blockers to original completion.
